post_topic: The open platform/DevOps seat that stalls the roadmap while the search drags on
scene_description: A split-scene showing two overloaded senior engineers at their desks buried under overlapping work — Slack alert windows, Terraform files, and Jira boards — while a conspicuously empty desk with a dormant monitor sits in the background, its chair pushed in and a job requisition printout pinned above it. On the right side, Kelvin Davis — a Black/African American man in his late 30s to 40s, short hair with grey at the temples and a neatly trimmed beard — sits at a laptop displaying the Cloud Decoded interface, a single human-in-the-loop approval gate visible on screen, governing the same pipeline work the other two are drowning in. The tension is between the structural tax of an unfilled DevOps seat spreading silently across the remaining team and the efficiency of one engineer using agentic tooling to govern what used to require three.
